title: Asked why the synth has no cat, a maker adds a cat voice to a folk quartet
summary: On Fri 13 Nov at 22:04Z @norvid-studies.bsky.social posted "concept: chimera vocal synth but for cats", quoting a photo of a cat posted by @goose.art. @yonderdavid.bsky.social (971 followers) replied with a screenshot of the synth's readme, which lists a "Bestiary: songbird (two-voice syrinx), seal, alligator and elephant", and at 22:36Z posted a video sample of those animal voices. @norvid-studies.bsky.social replied "genuinely how did cat not make the top 4 here". On Sat 14 Nov at 21:01Z, 21 hours later, the maker posted a video: per its alt text, "A quartet of chimera-vocal-synth voices, plus a physically simulated feline voice, sing "Poor Wayfaring Stranger," accompanied by physically simulated guitar and fiddle." It has 65 likes, 7 reposts and 9 quotes. In replies the maker described the work: the plan was a quartet of male voices; "The meow and yowl took some work and iteration against reference recordings. The original yowl sounded like a kazoo."; the first idea had been for the seal voice to hum bass on a different song, dropped over copyright; and the lead singer was meant to end by "expressing anger at the cat", which was dropped because the yowls "fit well enough that the cat deserved no such anger." Asked on Sat 14 Nov at 22:28Z to do another song, "Factory Girl", the maker posted it on Mon 16 Nov at 03:52Z, 29 hours later, with two heads, two fiddles and a cello, and an account of using three other models to get the voices to work.

couldBeShown: Four singing heads and a cat voice that meows and yowls in the arrangement; a guitar and a fiddle whose sound comes from physical simulation; the animal voices from the readme (songbird, seal, alligator, elephant) as a sample. The data describes the videos only through the alt texts quoted here; whether a cat is drawn on screen is not stated. The exchange in the thread is a run of short questions and answers between two accounts.

sensitive: @norvid-studies.bsky.social is marked featuredPrevious: spoke, so the account is not cast to speak in this episode; its posts may be shown. Eight of the 22 posts carried here are that account's, including every question the maker answers. @hailey.at has 45,295 followers; the scope review asks research to apply R7 to large accounts, and this is a single quote post of the video. @shimmermathlabs.com is marked featuredPrevious: shown. The maker's remarks about "male voices" and "feminine voices" are about the synthesizer's timbres, not about people. "Poor Wayfaring Stranger" is a spiritual; the maker calls it "an older melancholic folk song". Left out: a branch about copyright law that ends on a keyword-flagged remark; a question about the maker's musical training and the answer (offline life, R1); replies by @kumavis.me, whom the scope review identifies as the show's owner. The same maker is the subject of three other cards in this lane.
